summary.headline: Kranti Industries Q2 FY27 revenue rose 16.4% YoY to ₹25.16 crore, with gross margin at 54.3% and PAT of ₹56 lakh versus a Q1 loss.
summary.overview: Q2 FY27 revenue from operations was ₹25.16 crore (up about 16.4% YoY) and gross profit was ₹13.67 crore (up 33.8%), with gross margin expanding to 54.3% from 47.2%. EBITDA was ₹3.8 crore, flat-to-down against ₹4.0 crore a year ago but up 32.2% sequentially, with margin at 15.1% versus 11.3% in Q1. PAT was ₹56 lakh against a ₹5 lakh loss in Q1. H1 FY27 EBITDA fell to ₹6.68 crore from ₹7.23 crore as margins compressed on fixed costs, finance costs and depreciation. Management framed the quarter as a sequential recovery and highlighted new capacity at Jaipur ramping up.

segments.name: Jaipur plant
segments.commentary: Newly operational; capacity utilisation about 55-65% per management (figures differ within the call), targeted above 75% by end of Q3 and Q4 FY27. Expected revenue ₹9-10 crore in FY27 and ₹15-17 crore in FY28.

segments.name: EV products
segments.commentary: Management expects EV to be about 15-16% of revenue in FY28. Company says it has been in EV components since 2016.

segments.name: Defence
segments.commentary: Newly started work on defence products, described as a new category entry.

guidance_outlook: Two-digit revenue growth expected consistently for the next 2-3 years, split roughly 50:50 between existing and new customers and new segments.
Blended EBITDA margin targeted at 17.5-18% by end of FY27 or early FY28, from the current ~12.5-13% level, as new capacity stabilises and product mix improves.
Inventory to fall from more than 141 days to 121 days or lower (target under 100 days) by end of FY27; a 25-30 day reduction is targeted, with working-capital cash benefit.
Next two-year expansion plan to be released by end of Q3 FY27, pending customer FY27/FY28 volume projections. FY27 capex already largely committed.
Industry: auto-component domestic sales seen growing 7-8% annually to FY30; tractor volumes +1-4% in FY27; construction and mining equipment volumes +8-10% in FY27 (ICRA).
capex_capacity: Jaipur plant has started operations; utilisation about 65% (CEO) or 55% (Q&A), with break-even and above 75% targeted by end of Q3 and Q4 FY27.
Pune plant utilisation above 75%; blended utilisation about 65% per management.
FY27 expansion described as essentially complete; only a few machines already ordered and due to be added in FY27.
Machine ordering, testing and trials run 3-4 quarters ahead, so the next 2-year expansion plan is due by end of Q3 FY27.
demand_pricing: Management cites added product range: more than 100 new products and two new categories in the last two years, with defence now an entry area.

Product portfolio focused on transmission, gearboxes, hydraulic systems, transmission axles and braking systems for vehicles and construction/agri equipment; management says this is relevant across EV, hybrid and hydrogen fuel-cell platforms.
Receivables and payables described as comfortable; inventory elevated due to product variety, new products and tooling.
Management did not disclose specific pricing or realisation data; gross margin gain attributed to cost optimisation, inventory management and efficiency.

qa_highlights.question: Is the company expanding internationally?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is working on multiple fronts but declined to give details at this stage.

qa_highlights.question: Plans for new product categories or industries?
qa_highlights.answer: More than 100 new products and two new categories added in the last two years; defence work started this year.

qa_highlights.question: Split of future growth between existing and new customers?
qa_highlights.answer: Two-digit growth expected for 2-3 years, roughly 50:50 between existing and new customers and segments; adding products for existing customers is also treated as diversification.

qa_highlights.question: Jaipur plant outlook for FY27 and FY28?
qa_highlights.answer: Utilisation about 65%, expected above 75% by end of Q3 and Q4; revenue ₹9-10 crore in FY27 and ₹15-17 crore in FY28.

qa_highlights.question: Expected return on the recent capacity expansion?
qa_highlights.answer: EBITDA currently about 12.5-13%, expected to reach 17.5-18% blended by end-2026 or early 2027 with new mix and fixed-cost absorption.

qa_highlights.question: Current utilisation across plants and FY27 expansion plans?
qa_highlights.answer: Jaipur about 55%, Pune above 75%, blended about 65%; FY27 expansion already done, with next two-year plan due by end of Q3.

qa_highlights.question: Target for working capital cycle?
qa_highlights.answer: Inventory above 141 days to be cut to 121 days or lower, under 100 days in the longer term; reduction of 25-30 days targeted by end of FY27.

qa_highlights.question: EV contribution by FY28?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects EV at about 15-16% of revenue in FY28.

risks_watch: Operating leverage: fixed overheads, finance costs and rising depreciation kept H1 EBITDA margin at 13.2% versus 17.3% a year ago.
Inventory at more than 141 days ties up working capital; the 121-day and sub-100-day targets depend on execution by FY27 end.
The Jaipur ramp-up (utilisation ~55-65% now) must reach break-even and above 75% as planned to meet the ₹9-10 crore FY27 revenue estimate.
Management gave conflicting Jaipur utilisation figures (65% in prepared remarks vs 55% in Q&A) and an unquantified 17.5-18% EBITDA target; clarity needed next quarter.
Next two-year expansion plan (due end Q3 FY27) and defence and EV ramp timelines are not yet quantified.
summary.management_tone: Confident on sequential recovery and long-term growth, but cautious on profitability, acknowledging that "there is still room for improvement". Management was evasive on international expansion, declining to give details, and gave few hard numbers on pricing or realisations.
key_quotes: Overall, Q2 FY27 reflected a positive sequential improvement in our operating performance.
While there is still room for improvement, we are encouraged by the direction in which our operating performance is moving.
Our objective is not merely to grow revenue but to build a stronger and more profitable business with sustainable margins and long-term value creation for all our stakeholders.

growth.why: Management guides about two-digit revenue growth for the next 2-3 years, backed by the newly started Jaipur plant (FY27 revenue ₹9-10 crore, FY28 ₹15-17 crore, utilisation ~55-65% targeted above 75% by end Q3/Q4 FY27), a few machines due in FY27, and new products/defence entry; a specific expansion plan is only due by end Q3 FY27, so backing is partial.

quality.why: Q2 FY27 revenue grew 16.4% YoY to ₹25.16 crore, but the brief does not say whether volume or price drove it (management gave no pricing or realisation data and attributed the margin gain to cost optimisation), and it reports no one-off items in the quarter or the year-ago base.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Blended EBITDA margin at ~12.5-13% (Q2 15.1%) targeted at 17.5-18% by end FY27 or early FY28 as new capacity stabilises and mix improves, though H1 margin fell to 13.2% from 17.3% and management gave no quantified bridge.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Jaipur plant is commissioned at ~55-65% utilisation with a target above 75% by end Q3/Q4 FY27 and FY28 revenue of ₹15-17 crore; only a few machines are due in FY27, so new capacity is mostly ramp-up rather than new plants.

rows.label: Volume growth

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Next two-year expansion plan is due by end Q3 FY27 pending customer volume projections, while blended utilisation of ~65% (Pune above 75%) and FY27 expansion described as essentially complete.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Jaipur FY27 revenue guidance was pared to ₹9-10 crore and the 17.5-18% margin target is unquantified against H1 EBITDA margin of 13.2%, so the call does not point to an upgrade.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Jaipur must go from ~55-65% to above 75% utilisation to hit the ₹9-10 crore FY27 estimate, and H1 EBITDA fell to ₹6.68 crore from ₹7.23 crore on fixed costs, finance costs and depreciation.

rows.label: New product launch
